Tucson, Arizona · off the bike

Tucson off the bike: record stores, bookshops, bars

What to do in Tucson with the afternoon after the ride.

For: El Tour de Tucson.

Tucson off the bike: record stores, bookshops, bars, listed

What do you need?

  1. Pueblo Vida Brewing Company

    Downtown brewery taproom on Broadway, on the same block as the AC Hotel.

    • Bar
    • 115 East Broadway Boulevard, Tucson, AZ, 85701
    DirectionsWebsite
    More about Pueblo Vida Brewing Company

    A few bike racks by the door, and its own page says to ask the bartender where to put the bike inside if they’re full. No kitchen, so bring food in; leashed dogs welcome. Open 3 to 9 Monday to Thursday, noon to 10 Friday and Saturday, noon to 8 Sunday.

  2. Heirloom Farmers Market at Rillito Park

    At Rillito Park on the north side, right on the Rillito stretch of the Loop.

    • Market
    • 4502 N 1st Ave, Tucson, AZ 85718
    DirectionsWebsite
    More about Heirloom Farmers Market at Rillito Park

    Sundays year-round: 80-plus Southern Arizona farmers, ranchers and food makers, three shade pavilions and public restrooms. Visit Tucson lists 9 to 1 in winter and 8 to noon in summer; the market’s own site has the switch date. Ride to it, eat, ride on.

  3. Wooden Tooth Records (Congress Street)

    Downtown, with a beer and wine bar in the shop.

    • Record store
    • 108 E. Congress Street, Tucson, AZ 85701
    DirectionsWebsite
    More about Wooden Tooth Records (Congress Street)

    New and used vinyl, CDs, cassettes, books and turntables. Open noon to 8 Monday to Wednesday, noon to 7 Thursday, 11 to 10 Friday and Saturday, 11 to 6 Sunday; the first store, at 426 E. 7th Street, closes at 6 on weekdays.

  4. Antigone Books

    Fourth Avenue’s independent feminist bookstore: general, regional and feminist titles, cards and author events.

    • Bookstore
    • 411 N 4th Ave, Tucson, AZ 85705
    DirectionsWebsite
    More about Antigone Books

    Tuesday to Saturday 10 to 5, Sunday 11 to 4, closed Monday, per its GayTucson listing (June 2026); check the hours on antigonebooks.com. A Sunday afternoon after the long ride.

  5. IBT’s Bar + Food

    Fourth Avenue’s gay bar and dance club, open since 1985.

    • Bar
    • 616 North 4th Avenue, Tucson, AZ 85705
    DirectionsWebsite
    More about IBT’s Bar + Food

    Its own site says it was voted Tucson’s best gay bar. A patio, a big dance floor, drag shows Thursday through Saturday at 9 p.m. and a Sunday show from 1 to 3 p.m. Open noon to 2 a.m. every day.

  6. Arizona-Sonora Desert Museum

    West side, on Kinney Road in the Tucson Mountains, on the Gates Pass side of town.

    • Museum
    • 2021 N. Kinney Rd., Tucson AZ 85743
    DirectionsWebsite
    More about Arizona-Sonora Desert Museum

    Part zoo, part botanical garden, mostly outdoors; it says to plan at least two hours. Open 8:30 to 5 every day October to May; adults $29.95 (Oct 2026). No bike parking stated.

Checked October 3, 2026. No paid placements. Businesses open and close; call before you count on anyone.
